holidays.name: National Tartan Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate all things plaid-ish and Scottish, when people proudly don tartan kilts, scarves, and ties and the bagpipes come out to play.
holidays.origin: The U.S. Senate designated April 6 as National Tartan Day in 1997, and it was formally recognized in 2005. The date marks the signing of the Declaration of Arbroath in 1320, Scotland's declaration of independence.
holidays.funFact: New York City hosts a Tartan Day Parade featuring hundreds of pipers, and Canada celebrates its own Tartan Day on April 6 too.

holidays.name: National Caramel Popcorn Day
holidays.description: A sticky, crunchy salute to popcorn drenched in buttery caramel, perfect for movie nights, fairground nostalgia, and ruining your dental work.
holidays.origin: This unofficial food holiday grew out of the American snack tradition that took off with Cracker Jack, which debuted in the late 1800s and made caramel-coated popcorn a household favorite.
holidays.funFact: Cracker Jack was mentioned in the 1908 song 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game,' making it one of the few snacks immortalized in a baseball anthem.

holidays.name: New Beer's Eve
holidays.description: The night before the anniversary of the end of Prohibition-era beer bans, when fans of suds gather to toast the 'new' beer that is about to be legal again.
holidays.origin: On April 6, 1933, the day before the Cullen-Harrison Act took effect on April 7, Americans stocked up and celebrated the return of legal beer with 3.2% alcohol content after years of Prohibition.
holidays.funFact: When beer became legal again, Budweiser sent a team of Clydesdales to deliver a case to the White House, starting a long-running marketing tradition.

holidays.name: World Table Tennis Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to ping pong, the sport where tiny balls fly at alarming speeds and basements everywhere become Olympic arenas.
holidays.origin: The International Table Tennis Federation established World Table Tennis Day in 2015 to promote the sport worldwide, choosing April 6 to mark the date of the first World Table Tennis Championships in 1926.
holidays.funFact: Table tennis balls can spin at over 9,000 revolutions per minute, and the sport was once banned in the Soviet Union for a time over health concerns.

holidays.name: International Day of Sport for Development and Peace
holidays.description: A global celebration of using sports, from soccer to hopscotch, as a tool to bring people together and promote peace and understanding.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly declared April 6 as the day in 2013, selecting it because the first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens on April 6, 1896.
holidays.funFact: The 1896 Athens Olympics featured just 14 nations and about 241 athletes, and winners received silver medals and olive branches instead of gold.
